newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minority govt assured of budget approval.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minority govt assured of budget approval.

text.p: Portugal's minority Socialist government said on Wednesday that it had struck a deal with a small opposition party that ensured its budget programme passes parliament.

Prime Minister Antonio Guterres announced the accord on the budget -- which is vital to Portugal's chances of qualifying for the single currency -- after meeting Manuel Monteiro, leader of the right-wing Popular Party (PP).
"The accord...is that the PP is going to ensure that the budget passes in the final vote," Guterres told journalists.
Monteiro said that his party had succeeded in getting some tax concessions from the government in return for letting the budget pass when parliament votes next week.
"(Taxes) still have not gone down as far as the PP wants, but they are going to go down significantly thanks to the serious and responsible attitude of the PP," he said.

Guterres said that the Popular Party would not necessarily vote in favour of the budget because an abstention would be enough. The Popular Party has 15 representatives in the 230-seat chamber where the government is four seats short of an outright majority.
The 1997 budget cuts the deficit in line with targets for joining European economic and monetary union in 1999 and its eventual approval by parliament has never really been in doubt.
The largest opposition party, the Social Democrats, who share the Socialists' commitment to Europe, abstained when parliament voted on the general outlines of the plan last month.
The party has still to say what it will do on December 12 when parliament votes on the individual measures contained in the budget package.
